title: The Loch Arkaig Gold
subtitle: Loch Arkaig, Scottish Highlands · 1746

beats.vo: Scottish Highlands, seventeen forty-six. Weeks after Culloden, two French ships landed gold on the west coast for the Jacobite cause.

facts.claim: Place/year: the gold was hidden near Loch Arkaig in the Scottish Highlands in 1746 ('LOCH ARKAIG · 1746'). The ships themselves landed on the west coast at Loch nan Uamh / Arisaig, about 20 miles away, so the VO does not say the ships reached Loch Arkaig.

'Weeks after Culloden': the battle was 16 April 1746; the ships arrived after it. Landing dates disagree (Spink 29 Apr, Wikipedia 30 Apr, West Highland Museum 3 May, Ancient Origins 10 May), so the VO says only 'weeks after'. Coast.scot: 'a couple of weeks after'; WHM: 'two weeks after'.

Two French ships, the Mars and the Bellona (Bellone), brought money to fund the Jacobite cause; it is described as Spanish money (Wikipedia, Hidden Scotland 'funds and supplies from France and Spain', coast.scot 'Spain sent money'), in Louis d'or (Spink, WHM). VO says only 'gold for the Jacobite cause'. Amount deliberately not given: sources disagree (1,200,000 livres per Wikipedia/Express/Ancient Origins; 36,000 louis d'or per WHM; GBP 35,000 per Spink).
'The rising was already lost': the money arrived after the Jacobite defeat at Culloden.

Seven caskets of gold came ashore; one was stolen almost at once (Wikipedia: stolen by men of a named clan chief, deliberately not named; Hidden Scotland: 'One was almost immediately stolen'; Express 2024: seven caskets, one stolen).
The other six were carried inland (about 20 miles overland per Ancient Origins) and hidden/buried near Loch Arkaig.

'Only a few men knew where': coast.scot: hiding place known 'only to a few trusted Jacobite supporters'; Wikipedia/Ancient Origins: Murray of Broughton knew the secret, then it passed to Lochiel and then to Cluny Macpherson. Names deliberately left out of VO.

Some of the money reached Bonnie Prince Charlie in France (he escaped to France in Sept 1746); Spink/Downer: about GBP 6,000 was dug up, carried to London and sent on as notes to the Prince in France.

'Over the rest, his followers accused one another': coast.scot: survivors 'accused those who knew the secret of theft and embezzlement'; Hidden Scotland: 'Fingers were pointed', chiefs accused of misappropriating it; Wikipedia/Ancient Origins: claims and counter-claims, Charles accused Cluny of embezzlement. No individual named or accused in VO/caption; Archibald Cameron's 1753 return and execution deliberately left out (violence).
Gold coins later turned up in nearby woods: Clan Cameron records mention French gold coins found buried in nearby woods in the 1850s ('later'; caption '1850s').

'Some say the rest was gone long ago': Spink (Martyn Downer, 2020) says the rest had 'already been pilfered or given away in the Highlands' and 'it isn't there'; Sunday Telegraph 2 Aug 2020 'There's no gold in them thar hills after all'; Hidden Scotland: Cluny told Charles it had all been used. Softened to 'gone' (covers spent, taken, given away).

'If it is still there, it has never been found': Undiscovered Scotland: 'the hiding place, it is said, has never been found'; coast.scot: 'If the treasure is there, it is still to be discovered'; WHM: 'the gold has not been found'; Ancient Origins: bulk still unlocated.

Still unsolved as of Nov 2026: Scottish Daily Express (20 Aug 2024) says the haul 'seems to have disappeared' and may still be around Loch Arkaig; no 2024-2026 report of the hoard being found (searched Nov 2026: only unrelated Culloden projectile finds, Univ. of Glasgow / NTS Oct 2025). Undiscovered Scotland (current page) and coast.scot still describe it as never found. Caveat: Spink/Downer (2020) claims 'the mystery has been solved, it isn't there' (i.e. spent/taken, not found) — hence the 'if it is still there' phrasing.
